title: DouglasRachfordSmoothConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize f(x)+g(x) over convex C in a real Hilbert space. The function f is differentiable and globally convex; g is convex on C. A constrained minimizer exists.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The objective combines a globally L-smooth convex function f with a possibly nonsmooth convex term g restricted to C.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Exact proximal minimizers at the fixed public parameter γ: proxF minimizes f(x)+‖x−w‖²/(2γ) over E; proxG minimizes g(y)+‖y−v‖²/(2γ) over C and returns a feasible point. Exactness holds for every call index and seed. No direct gradient or function-value queries are supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: unknown_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: L is hidden from the algorithm, while γ and λ are public and certify L≤λ/(4γ). Valid parameters satisfy L,γ,R,ε>0 and 0<λ≤1. R and ε are also hidden; the execution budget may depend on them.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DouglasRachfordSmoothConvex.lean: Public; Params; spec.publicInput; spec.valid. LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Initialization is bounded relative to a shifted minimizer: for some constrained minimizer x*, ‖w1−(x*+γ∇f(x*))‖≤R. E may be infinite-dimensional. Closedness of C and lower semicontinuity of g are not explicitly required; exact proximal minimizers must exist for every query.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point satisfies f(output)+g(output)−f(x*)−g(x*)≤ε for a constrained minimizer x*. No averaging or particular iterate is prescribed.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point belongs to C.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the ε objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within a fixed worst-case oracle budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is standard smooth composite convex minimization with exact proximal access in Hilbert space, a shifted-solution initialization bound, and a feasible objective-gap target.

descriptionHtml:
Smooth Convex Proximal Minimization

We consider minimizing f+g over a convex set C in a real Hilbert space E, where f,g:E→R. The function f is differentiable, convex, and smooth with a hidden constant L>0, while g is convex on C. For a given proximal parameter γ>0, the oracle returns exact proximal minimizers of f over E and of g over C. A given point w1∈E satisfies ∥w1−(x⋆+γ∇f(x⋆))∥≤R for some minimizer x⋆∈C and radius R>0. For ε>0, the goal is a feasible output x¯ with (f+g)(x¯)−(f+g)(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

Write F(x)=f(x)+g(x). The optimization problem is minx∈CF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The parameters satisfy L>0,γ>0,0<λ≤1,4γL≤λ,R>0,ε>0. The algorithm receives only E, γ, λ, and w1; the remaining parameters L, R, and ε may enter only the oracle-call budget.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E. For all x,y∈E, f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩≤f(y),f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L2∥y−x∥2. The set C is convex, and g is convex on C: for all x,y∈C and t∈[0,1], g((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)g(x)+tg(y).

Assumption 2 (Exact proximal access). For every w,v∈E, the oracle returns the respective minimizers pf(w)∈argminx∈E{f(x)+∥x−w∥22γ},pg(v)∈argminy∈C{g(y)+∥y−v∥22γ}. Both minimizers exist for every query point. Either type of query may be made anywhere in E, and both types count toward a single total oracle-call budget.

Assumption 3 (Minimizer and initial distance). There exists x⋆∈C such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈C,∥w1−(x⋆+γ∇f(x⋆))∥≤R.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy x¯∈C,F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Panagiotis Patrinos, Lorenzo Stella, Alberto Bemporad. Douglas-Rachford Splitting: Complexity Estimates and Accelerated Variants. 2014 (CDC publication; September 2014 preprint v2 used). Complexity: O(1+R(1+γL)/(γ(1−γL)ε)) exact proximal-oracle calls using fast Douglas–Rachford, counting both proximal evaluations per iteration, for objective gap ≤ε; 0<γL<1.
theorems.formulaHtml: 2⋅⌈2⋅R2lam⋅γ⋅ε⌉+

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space, f is differentiable and convex with the global quadratic upper bound of parameter L>0; C is convex and g is convex on C. Exact proximal minimizers of f and of g over C are available at fixed γ. A minimizer x⋆∈C exists with ∥w1−x⋆−γ∇f(x⋆)∥≤R. Assume R,ε,γ>0, 0<λ≤1, and 4γL≤λ. The constructed fast Douglas–Rachford method guarantees yN∈C and F(yN)−F(x⋆)≤ε deterministically for its last iterate.

Fast Douglas–Rachford splitting under the DouglasRachfordSmoothConvex setup.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) AcceleratedDouglasRachfordConvex (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O(1+Rλγε) proximal calls. At λ=1, γ=1/(4L): O(1+LR2/ε).
(2) Fast Douglas–Rachford (Patrinos et al. 2014, Theorem 5) O(1+Rλγε) proximal calls. Special case: finite-dimensional quadratic f, closed proper g+ιC; 0<γ<1/L, λ=(1−γL)/(1+γL). (1): Scope: extends the same method’s accelerated last-iterate guarantee to nonquadratic smooth convex f. Matches the rate on the quadratic overlap; no problem-class speedup established. (1) needs 4γL≤λ; excludes (2)’s optimal γ=(2−1)/L. Tuned finite-iteration constants are worse for N≤4.

Abbr: F=f+g on C; ιC is the convex indicator of C; L is the smoothness parameter; R bounds the initial distance to x⋆+γ∇f(x⋆); γ is the proximal parameter; λ is the relaxation; N is the iteration count; ε is the objective-gap tolerance. Costs count one evaluation of each proximal map per iteration.

Patrinos, Panagiotis, Lorenzo Stella, and Alberto Bemporad. 2014. “Douglas–Rachford Splitting: Complexity Estimates and Accelerated Variants.” 53rd IEEE Conference on Decision and Control, 4234–39. https://doi.org/10.1109/CDC.2014.7040049.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import LongTails.Template

open Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.DouglasRachfordSmoothConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  γ : ℝ
  lam : ℝ
  w1 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

structure Params extends Public where
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

inductive Query (p : Public) where
  | proxF (w : p.E)
  | proxG (v : p.E)

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  g : p.E → ℝ
  C : Set p.E

noncomputable def objective {p : Public} (I : Instance p) (x : p.E) : ℝ := I.f x + I.g x

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query := Query
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.γ ∧ 0 < q.lam ∧ q.lam ≤ 1 ∧ 4 * q.γ * q.L ≤ q.lam ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I oracle :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt I.f (gradient I.f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, I.f x + ⟪gradient I.f x, y - x⟫ ≤ I.f y) ∧
    (∀ x y, I.f y ≤ I.f x + ⟪gradient I.f x, y - x⟫ + q.L / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2) ∧
    Convex ℝ I.C ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ I.C I.g ∧
    (∀ k seed w, IsMinOn (fun x => I.f x + ‖x - w‖ ^ 2 / (2 * q.γ)) univ
      (oracle.answer k (0, (.proxF w)) seed)) ∧
    (∀ k seed v, oracle.answer k (0, (.proxG v)) seed ∈ I.C ∧
      IsMinOn (fun y => I.g y + ‖y - v‖ ^ 2 / (2 * q.γ)) I.C (oracle.answer k (0, (.proxG v)) seed)) ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.C, IsMinOn (objective I) I.C xstar ∧
      ‖q.w1 - (xstar + q.γ • gradient I.f xstar)‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q I output P :=
    ∃ xstar ∈ I.C, IsMinOn (objective I) I.C xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _),
        output ω ∈ I.C ∧ objective I (output ω) - objective I xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.DouglasRachfordSmoothConvex
